# nish/release

What the newest release of a project on GitHub is, whether it is newer than the one running, and a small cache so a program asks at most once a day.

```ts
import {
  ReleaseCache,
  ReleaseVersion,
  releaseBaseAllowed,
  releaseCacheFresh,
  releaseCacheParse,
  releaseCacheRead,
  releaseCacheWrite,
  releaseCheckCached,
  releaseCompare,
  releaseFetchInstaller,
  releaseFileTrusted,
  releaseIsNewer,
  releaseLatest,
  releaseParseVersion,
  releaseTagFromLocation,
  releaseValidVersion,
} from "nish/release";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { releaseCheckCached, releaseLatest } from "nish/release"

const latest: string | null = releaseLatest("https://github.com/owner/repo", 2000)
const newer: string | null = releaseCheckCached(
  "https://github.com/owner/repo", "1.2.0", "/home/me/.cache/app/latest", 86400000, 2000)
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-callout type="info">

- `releaseValidVersion(v)` — whether `v` is a version that may go in a URL:
  it starts with a digit and holds only letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `+`,
  with no `..`. The same rule as `install.sh`'s `nish_valid_version`.
- `releaseParseVersion(v)` and `releaseCompare(a, b)` — semantic versions,
  `major.minor.patch[-pre][+build]`. A prerelease sorts below its release
  and build metadata is ignored.
- `releaseIsNewer(candidate, current)` — true only when both parse and the
  candidate is strictly newer, so a version that does not parse is never
  newer and nothing here ever proposes a downgrade.
- `releaseTagFromLocation(base, location)` — the version a
  `/releases/latest` redirect names, or null for anything that is not
  exactly `<base>/releases/tag/v<version>`.
- `releaseLatest(base, timeoutMs)` — asks `<base>/releases/latest` once,
  without following the redirect, and answers its version or null. Every
  failure is null: a server that is down, slow, refuses, or answers
  anything but a redirect to a release tag.
- `releaseCacheRead`, `releaseCacheWrite` and `releaseCheckCached` — the
  answer kept in a file the program names, believed only when it is a
  regular file this user owns that no one else can write, and only for
  `maxAgeMs` (a check dated in the future counts as stale).
- `releaseFetchInstaller(rawBase, version, path)` — the `install.sh` of one
  release tag, written to a file for the caller to run, never piped into a
  shell.

</scalar-callout>

Nothing here runs under a wasm32 build: it reaches the network and reads file
owners. The record of what it defends against is `docs/security/release.md`.

## Functions

### releaseBaseAllowed

Whether `base` is a URL this module will ask: `https://`, or `http://` only
to this machine (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]`), which is what a test
server listens on.

```ts
function releaseBaseAllowed(base: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="string" required>

The URL.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the URL may be fetched.

</scalar-field>

### releaseCacheFresh

Whether a cache checked at `checkedMs` still answers at `nowMs`: younger
than `maxAgeMs`, and not dated in the future, which a clock set back or a
planted file would give.

```ts
function releaseCacheFresh(
  cache: ReleaseCache,
  nowMs: i64,
  maxAgeMs: i64,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="cache" type="ReleaseCache" required>

The cache.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nowMs" type="i64" required>

The time now, in milliseconds since 1970.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="maxAgeMs" type="i64" required>

How long an answer stays fresh.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the cache need not be refreshed.

</scalar-field>

function releaseCacheParse(

### releaseCacheRead

The cache at `path`, or null when there is none, it cannot be believed (see
`releaseFileTrusted`; its directory, too, must be a directory this user
owns that no one else can write, so nobody else can swap the file between
the check and the read) or it does not parse. Its format is two lines,
`checked <ms>` and `latest <version>`, the version empty when the check found
none.

```ts
function releaseCacheRead(
  path: string,
): ReleaseCache | null
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

The cache file.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="ReleaseCache | null">

What the cache holds, or null.

</scalar-field>

### releaseCacheWrite

Writes the cache at `path`: its directory is created mode 0700 when missing
(its parent must exist), the text goes to a new temporary file beside it of
mode 0600, and that is renamed over `path`, so a reader sees the old cache or
the new one and a link planted at `path` is replaced, never followed.

```ts
function releaseCacheWrite(
  path: string,
  latest: string,
  nowMs: i64,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

The cache file.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="latest" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nowMs" type="i64" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

</scalar-field>

### releaseCheckCached

The newest release when it is newer than `current`, from the cache at
`cachePath` while it is fresh and believed, else from `releaseLatest`, whose
answer (or its failure, as "") is written back so the next call within
`maxAgeMs` asks nothing.

```ts
function releaseCheckCached(
  base: string,
  current: string,
  cachePath: string,
  maxAgeMs: i64,
  timeoutMs: i32,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="string" required>

The repository URL, as `releaseLatest` takes it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="current" type="string" required>

The version running now.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="cachePath" type="string" required>

The cache file; its directory's parent must exist.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="maxAgeMs" type="i64" required>

How long an answer stays fresh, e.g. 86400000 for a day.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="timeoutMs" type="i32" required>

The most milliseconds a check may take.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The newer version, or null when there is none or none is known.

</scalar-field>

### releaseCompare

Two versions in semantic-version order: the numbers, then the prerelease,
where a prerelease sorts below its release; build metadata is ignored. A
version that does not parse sorts below every one that does, and two that do
not parse compare equal.

```ts
function releaseCompare(a: string, b: string): i32
```

<scalar-field name="a" type="string" required>

The first version, without a leading `v`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="string" required>

The second version, without a leading `v`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

-1, 0 or 1 as `a` is older than, the same as, or newer than `b`.

</scalar-field>

### releaseFetchInstaller

The `install.sh` of release `version`, fetched from
`<rawBase>/v<version>/install.sh` and written to `path`. It is the script of
that tag, never of a branch, and it goes to a file so the caller runs it with
`sh <path>` — nothing fetched is ever piped into a shell. `path` should be in
a directory only this user can write.

```ts
function releaseFetchInstaller(
  rawBase: string,
  version: string,
  path: string,
  timeoutMs: i32,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="rawBase" type="string" required>

The raw-content URL, e.g. `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo`: https, or http to this machine.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="version" type="string" required>

The release to fetch, without a `v`; refused unless `releaseValidVersion`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

Where to write the script.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="timeoutMs" type="i32" required>

The most milliseconds the whole request may take.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when a 200 answer was written to `path`.

</scalar-field>

### releaseFileTrusted

Whether the file at `path` may be believed: a regular file (a symbolic link
is not followed), owned by this process's effective user, and writable by
neither its group nor every user.

```ts
function releaseFileTrusted(path: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

The file.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the file may be read and believed.

</scalar-field>

### releaseIsNewer

Whether `candidate` is strictly newer than `current`. Both must parse: a
version that does not is never newer, and neither is the same release or an
older one, so the answer never suggests a downgrade.

```ts
function releaseIsNewer(
  candidate: string,
  current: string,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="candidate" type="string" required>

The version that might be newer.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="current" type="string" required>

The version running now.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True only when both parse and `candidate` is the newer.

</scalar-field>

### releaseLatest

The newest release of the repository at `base`, read from where
`<base>/releases/latest` redirects. The redirect is not followed and needs
no token. Null when the server cannot be reached within `timeoutMs`, answers
anything but a 3xx, or redirects anywhere but a release tag of `base`.

```ts
function releaseLatest(
  base: string,
  timeoutMs: i32,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="string" required>

The repository URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo`: https, or http to this machine.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="timeoutMs" type="i32" required>

The most milliseconds the whole request may take.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The newest version, without a `v`, or null.

</scalar-field>

### releaseParseVersion

`v` as a semantic version, `major.minor.patch` with an optional `-pre` and
`+build`, or null when it is not one. A leading `v` is not accepted; strip
it first.

```ts
function releaseParseVersion(
  v: string,
): ReleaseVersion | null
```

<scalar-field name="v" type="string" required>

The version text.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="ReleaseVersion | null">

The parsed version, or null.

</scalar-field>

### releaseTagFromLocation

The version a `/releases/latest` redirect names: `location` must be exactly
`<base>/releases/tag/v<version>`, and the version must parse. A redirect anywhere else — another repository, a login
page, the releases list when there is no release, a query or fragment — names
none.

```ts
function releaseTagFromLocation(
  base: string,
  location: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="string" required>

The repository URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo`, with no trailing slash.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="location" type="string" required>

The redirect's `Location` header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The version, without a `v`, or null.

</scalar-field>

### releaseValidVersion

Whether `v` may be put in a URL as a release version: not empty, starting
with a digit, holding only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `+`, and
never `..`. What it rules out is a version that reaches past the tag in a
path — a `/`, a `..`, a `?`, a `#`, a `%`, whitespace.

```ts
function releaseValidVersion(v: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="v" type="string" required>

The version, without a leading `v`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the version is safe to put in a release URL.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### ReleaseCache

The cache's contents: when the check ran and what it found.

```ts
class ReleaseCache
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ReleaseCache()` |  |
| `checkedMs: i64` | When the check ran, in milliseconds since 1970 (`Date.now()`'s clock). |
| `latest: string` | The version the check found, or "" when it found none. |

### ReleaseVersion

A parsed semantic version. `pre` is the prerelease after the `-`, empty for a
release; build metadata after the `+` is dropped, as it never orders.

```ts
class ReleaseVersion
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ReleaseVersion()` |  |
| `major: i64` | The major number. |
| `minor: i64` | The minor number. |
| `patch: i64` | The patch number. |
| `pre: string` | The prerelease identifiers, dot-separated, or "" for a release. |
